questions.stem: A is \(25\%\) more efficient than B. If B can complete a work in \(20\) days, in how many days can A and B together complete the same work?
questions.keySolution:
B’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{20}\)
A is \(25\%\) more efficient ⇒ A’s 1-day work = \(1.25 \times \tfrac{1}{20} = \tfrac{1}{16}\)
Combined 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{20} + \tfrac{1}{16} = \tfrac{9}{80}\)
Time together = \(\tfrac{1}{\tfrac{9}{80}} = \tfrac{80}{9}\) days

questions.stem: If \(30\%\) of a work is completed by A in \(12\) days, in how many days can A complete the entire work?
A and B together can complete \(60\%\) of a work in \(18\) days. If A alone can complete the work in \(50\) days, in how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
Whole work time together = \(\frac{18}{0.60} = 30\) days ⇒ combined 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{30}\)
A’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{50}\)
B’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{30} - \tfrac{1}{50} = \tfrac{1}{75}\)
∴ B alone finishes in \(75\) days

questions.stem: A machine works at \(80\%\) efficiency and completes a task in \(15\) days. If the efficiency is increased to \(100\%\), in how many days will the same task be completed?
P is \(50\%\) less efficient than Q. If P and Q together complete a work in \(12\) days, in how many days can Q alone complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
Let Q’s 1-day work = \(1\) unit ⇒ P’s = \(0.5\) unit
Together they do \(1.5\) units/day and finish work in \(12\) days ⇒ total work = \(18\) units
Q alone needs \(\tfrac{18}{1} = 18\) days

questions.stem: A completes \(40\%\) of a work in \(8\) days. B completes the remaining work in \(15\) days. In how many days can A and B together complete the entire work?
questions.keySolution:
A’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{0.40}{8} = \tfrac{1}{20}\)
B’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{0.60}{15} = \tfrac{1}{25}\)
Combined 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{20} + \tfrac{1}{25} = \tfrac{9}{100}\)
Time = \(\tfrac{1}{\tfrac{9}{100}} = \tfrac{100}{9}\) days

questions.stem: If \(75\%\) of a work can be completed by \(20\) men in \(30\) days, how many men are required to complete \(100\%\) of the work in \(25\) days?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(20 \times 30 \div 0.75 = 800\) man-days
Men needed for \(25\) days = \(\tfrac{800}{25} = 32\) men

questions.stem: A works with \(120\%\) efficiency compared to his normal rate and completes a job in \(10\) days. At normal efficiency, how many days would he take?
X and Y together complete \(80\%\) of a work in \(16\) days. If X alone can complete the full work in \(30\) days, what percentage of work can Y complete in \(12\) days?
A pipe can fill \(25\%\) of a tank in \(2\) hours. At the same rate, how long will it take to fill \(60\%\) of the tank?
Worker A completes \(30\%\) more work than worker B in the same time. If A completes a job in \(20\) days, how many days will B take to complete the same job?
questions.keySolution:
Let B’s 1-day work = \(1\) unit ⇒ A’s = \(1.3\) units
Total work = \(1.3 \times 20 = 26\) units
Time for B = \(\tfrac{26}{1} = 26\) days

questions.stem: A team completes \(45\%\) of a project in \(18\) days. At the same rate, how many more days are needed to complete the remaining project?
questions.keySolution:
Rate = \(\tfrac{45\%}{18} = 2.5\%\) per day
Remaining work = \(55\%\)
Additional days = \(\tfrac{55}{2.5} = 22\) days

questions.stem: If \(40\%\) of workers are removed from a project, leaving \(36\) workers to finish it, how many workers were originally employed?
A machine operating at \(90\%\) efficiency completes a task in \(24\) hours. If efficiency drops to \(75\%\), how many additional hours are needed to complete the task?
P and Q together can complete \(70\%\) of a work in \(14\) days. If P alone can complete the entire work in \(40\) days, in how many days can Q alone complete \(50\%\) of the work?
questions.keySolution:
Full-work time together = \(\tfrac{14}{0.70} = 20\) days ⇒ combined 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{20}\)
P’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{40}\)
Q’s 1-day work = \(\tfrac{1}{20} - \tfrac{1}{40} = \tfrac{1}{40}\)
Time for Q to finish \(50\%\) work = \(0.5 \times 40 = 20\) days
